page: Vultr voc-m-16c-128gb-3200s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute server featuring 16 dedicated vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC processor. Built on the x86_64 architecture, this instance provides 8 physical cores with 2 threads per core running at a base frequency of 2.0 GHz, supported by a 32 MB L3 cache. The hardware configuration includes 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Storage is bundled as a local 3200 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU accelerators are present on this server.

In benchmark testing, the server demonstrates strong memory performance and competitive compute capabilities. The PassMark memory score ranks in the top tier, supported by strong uncached large-block memory read bandwidth of 340.0 GB/sec and write bandwidth of 160.84 GB/sec. Single-core CPU performance via stress-ng is also in the top tier, while multi-core CPU performance and PassMark CPU scores align with the average tier. For database and web workloads, the system achieves an average of 38.03 million Redis SET operations per second and a static web serving throughput of 15.74 GB/sec. Small-model LLM text generation is strong at 315.31 tokens per second.

This server offers a balanced resource density for memory-intensive and storage-heavy workloads without the premium of specialized bare-metal hardware. The high memory capacity combined with a generous 3200 GB NVMe SSD makes it highly cost-efficient for hosting relational databases, in-memory caching systems, and data-intensive applications. However, the 2.0 GHz CPU clock speed presents a tradeoff, resulting in average multi-core compute scaling compared to higher-frequency compute-optimized instances. It is best suited for memory-optimized databases, medium-scale ETL pipelines, and web serving environments requiring substantial local storage.
